open_questions: TESS centroid inconclusive (no difference image) leaves neighbour blend formally open despite flat bottom and steady depth; one neighbour at 17.7 arcsec plausibles within 1px with 0.1569 eclipse needed
Transit depths p_consistent 0.026072 with share_of_top_3 0.948 indicate top transit dominates; more follow-up transits needed to confirm consistency

Rotation sectors show amplitude 8990-11227 ppm and period aliases but signal at 12.4 d not at integer multiple (signal_over_rotation 1.626...) with no phase-curve overbump, so variability does not explain flat 6508 ppm dip
dossier.public_summary: A 3.6 Earth-radius flat-bottomed transit repeats every 12.4 days with duration, depth and flat shape consistent with a planet around an M dwarf and shows no secondary eclipse or odd-even change. The depth is steady across sectors and the signal persists above noise despite faint star and one close neighbour within one TESS pixel. The best explanation is a small to medium planet, pending radial velocities and on-target confirmation to rule out a very diluted binary blend.

reasons.why: Observed 2.5 h vs central 2.333 h fits M dwarf with b=0.07; stellar_radius confirms ratio 0.97-1.07 for 0.409-0.456 R_sun, size 3.62-4.04 R_earth.
Flat-bottomed (not V-shaped) with ingress_fraction 0.05 favours uniform disk transit, not grazing EB.
Depth steady across sectors 55,81,92 (6288, 5835, 6286 ppm, chi2 0.07451) despite contratio 0.01068, argues against blend/contamination variability.
Secondary below 5-sigma and secondary_over_bump 1.169, with best_brightening_snr 2.893, no significant secondary argues against stellar companion; odd_even diff_sigma null.
Signal detected at SNR 10.25 with 4 transits, mean depth 6161 ppm, size 3.621 R_earth in planet regime, moderate xgboost rank 0.08 offset.
